provenance.method: BENCH_ROUNDS=150 BENCH_CORE=13,15 pnpm benchValidate on ark/repo/bench, on a shared machine, each run started below a 1-minute load of 4 (2.9-3.9 at the runs' starts and ends), benchmark processes pinned to cores 13 and 15. Each library runs in its own process, driven round by round over IPC; one arm is timed at a time and the arm order rotates each round. Each arm warms 1 s / 10k calls, then a sample is the mean ns per call over a batch of >= 0.5 ms, on fresh unfrozen copies of the input. Every arm's output is checked to agree with arktype's before timing. Medians are over rounds; p is a two-sided sign test paired by round; verdict is win/loss at p < .05, else tie. replication tallies the same comparison's verdict in 1 further quiet run at the same commit.
provenance.size: esbuild-minified bundle of each app at f29b8d153, bytes and gzip

startup.method: median over one quiet pass of fresh Node processes, each importing an app's esbuild-minified bundle and validating once

arms.standalone: arktype precompiled to a standalone validator (default build: errors "all"), on arktype/runtime
arms.arktype: arktype's runtime JIT (type() at startup, compiled with new Function)
arms.zodCompiled: zod 4.6.7 z.compile(schema) (.safeParse; .validate for allows); on invalid rows its compiled check, then zod's runtime parser for the issues; on parse tree zod's runtime parser, since z.compile refuses recursive schemas
arms.typia: typia 15.1.0, AOT via ttsc (createValidate; createIs for allows; createAssert for first; validatePrune for strip; validateEquals for strict)
arms.valibot: valibot 1.5.0 (safeParse; is for allows; abortEarly for first)
arms.ajv: ajv 8.20.0 (compile; allErrors for issues/errors; removeAdditional for strip; useDefaults)
arms.typebox: TypeBox 1.3.37 (Compile: Check; Clean+Check for strip; Default+Check for defaults; Decode for morph; Errors for invalid rows)

caveats: zod (classic, compiled, mini) and valibot's parse rows build a new output object (their default object mode strips undeclared keys); arktype, typia, ajv and TypeBox return the input. The strip rows are the like-for-like comparison with that behavior.

Rows where another library beats the precompiled arm in both runs: compiled zod on parse items morph and parse moltar morph (it builds its output as it transforms; arktype copies each object it changes), ajv on parse items defaults, and ajv on the moltar invalid rows and errors and first product.
ajv and TypeBox's Check return a boolean, not the data. typia's createValidate allocates a { success, data, errors } result per call.
arktype's errors/first rows read .summary, which writes every message; issues rows read the raw errors.
The sign test can't see a bias that holds for a whole run (such as the core a process settled on), so a verdict counts when it replicates.

scenarios.measures: the same object with undeclared keys rejected at both levels; the valid input has none, so this is the cost of looking for them

scenarios.name: product

scenarios.name: items

scenarios.name: discriminated
scenarios.measures: a 4-branch object union keyed on `kind`, inputs cycling through every branch (zod discriminatedUnion, valibot variant, ajv discriminator; arktype discriminates on its own)

scenarios.name: rotating
scenarios.measures: 8 small validators (string, non-empty string, two 1-key objects, number, string[], a 2-object union, a bounded number) called in turn from one call site, as a shared helper would call them

scenarios.name: constraints
scenarios.measures: one object of refinements: string length bounds, email format (each library's own regex), integer range, exclusive bound, a regex pattern

scenarios.name: morph
scenarios.measures: parse a numeric string to a number ("12345" -> 12345); typia and ajv can't transform

scenarios.name: defaults
scenarios.measures: an object missing 2 defaulted and 2 optional keys; the output must hold the defaults (typia has none)

scenarios.name: items morph
scenarios.measures: 100 items { id, name, count }, each count a numeric string parsed to a number: a transform below the root, which a library copies or writes into its input

scenarios.name: items defaults
scenarios.measures: 100 items { id, name }, each missing a defaulted boolean the output must hold

scenarios.name: moltar morph
scenarios.measures: moltar's object with its nested `num` a numeric string parsed to a number

scenarios.name: tree
scenarios.measures: a recursive { id, children: node[] } tree, depth 3, 3 children per node (40 nodes)
